input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Mutuality, the mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, all carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and the payment-obligation exclusion are already in place in §§ 21.1–21.3. The cap basis, however, is illusory: it keys to "Fees", defined in § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee, i.e. the one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form (§ 1.6), and is further limited to the first Order Form. That is not 12 months of fees and sits below the walk-away threshold of a Vendor cap below six months' fees. One surgical edit to § 21.1 moves the basis to the greater of fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000, leaving all other retained mechanics verbatim.

proposal.summary: Fix illusory cap basis: greater of 12 months' fees under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap currently keys to "Fees", defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so it is illusory. We have moved it to our position: the greater of fees paid or payable under the Agreement in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000, with Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) remaining outside the cap.
